### Upload collections retain originals and file history

Upload collections now store `original` metadata and a `prefix` and `_objectKey` for each stored file (the main file, `original`, and each variant), so saved versions can find their files. New uploads keep their uploaded filename. With a storage adapter, each new file is stored under its own `_objectKey` folder, so update any code or infrastructure that relies on the old object key. When a processed main file and its original share a filename, request the original with `?original=true`; `original.url` already includes it. With local storage, the original gets a counter name instead (for example `photo-1.png`). Files saved by earlier v4 beta releases with an `-original` filename keep that name and are still served. Custom storage adapters should handle the new `params.isOriginal` in `staticHandler`; see [Custom Storage Adapters](../upload/storage-adapters#custom-storage-adapters).

-**Postgres and SQLite:** after updating, run `payload migrate:create`, check that it adds these columns to each upload collection table and its versions table, then run `payload migrate`. Existing rows keep `null` values until their next write.

Upload collections also have a core-controlled `_stored` field on the main file, on `original`, and on each entry under `variants`. A value of `false` marks an entry with no stored object. A missing or `null` value means stored, so existing documents need no data backfill. Payload ignores client writes to this field. It is hidden in the Admin Panel, but can appear in API responses; it is not a field-level hidden value. See [Files with no stored default](../upload/transformers#files-with-no-stored-default).

`_stored` is now reserved for these file entries. If an upload collection already defines a custom `_stored` field, rename it and move its data, including data in saved versions, before upgrading. Remove the old custom values from `_stored`: existing `false` values would otherwise be treated as files with no stored object, and writes to the custom field would be ignored.

-**Postgres and SQLite:** run `payload migrate:create`, check that it adds the `_stored` columns for file entries in each upload collection and its versions, then run `payload migrate`. Existing rows keep `null`.
